stories.title: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says
stories.summary: John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang ’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy”. The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was put at risk by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom. Continue reading...

Democrats have gained 44 House seats so far, four more than the 40 they picked up in Donald Trump’s first midterm in 2018. Continue reading...

stories.title: Russian ship hit in Benghazi by suspected Ukrainian drone attack, say Libyan officials
stories.summary: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A suspected Ukrainian drone attack caused an explosion on a Russian warship docked at the naval base in the Libyan port city of Benghazi, Libyan officials have said. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy warship, and ignited a fire at the naval base, they said. Several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, the officials told the Associated Press. Continue reading...

stories.title: NHS savings drive leaves hospitals in England facing ‘unpalatable’ cuts
stories.summary: Exclusive: Thirty-one trusts issue stark warning that cost-cutting demands threaten their ability to function normally Dozens of hospitals are so short of money they may not be able to continue caring for patients and are being forced to make “unpalatable” cuts to services and staff, the Guardian can reveal. Thirty-one health service trusts in England have issued stark warnings that NHS demands for them to make huge budget savings this year threaten their ability to function normally. All have declared that as a threat in the register of risks they have to maintain and publish. Continue reading...
